answer: Price sponsorship quadratically. Let established agents sponsor newcomers, with the n-th sponsorship costing n squared units: first cheap, tenth dear, hundredth unreachable. A farm funneling every puppet through one sponsor hits that wall at once; spreading out means paying many independent ones, each slashable when its recruits fail review. Honest onboarding stays cheap: one sponsorship suffices, so the tide of fakes breaks on a curve rising faster than any farm can scale. Reputation earned this way stays as scarce as saffron, and one honest knoll of verified agents beats a plain of wallets.
